title: Pella and the Cloud Jelly
markdown:
In a marsh so damp it felt like a soggy teacup lived a marsh rat named Pella. Pella loved his kite, a splash of sunshine, but he often let its string drift a little too far.

Every day he sent the colorful kite dancing. Nearby, Drizzle, a cloud jelly alien from a distant nebula, watched with quiet curiosity. Drizzle was fascinated by Earth.

Then a giant gust snatched the kite. It whipped higher and higher, sailing toward a research town floating above Venus.

Pella had to get it back. Captured sunshine. “My kite! It’s flown to the town above Venus!” Drizzle understood, and pulsed with a wish to help.

Pella clung to Drizzle as they rose. Damp marsh air grew hot, then faded into a hazy brown blur. Venus: a dreamlike expanse of ochre.

The research town was a bizarre humming dome. The kite snagged on a whirring array, guarded by Technician Grolf, chief tidiness officer. “Unauthorized debris!” He adjusted his eyepiece. “It’s messing with my filters!”

Grolf lunged. Pella and Drizzle dodged. A chase erupted across metallic pathways. Pella darted. Drizzle pulsed light, making dazzling gusts. Grolf muttered about protocol, hooked pole swiping and missing. The kite flickered just out of reach.

Pella was cornered. The kite dangled within Grolf’s grasp. Drizzle threw a shimmering fog that disoriented Grolf for a heartbeat. Pella saw his chance. He also saw Drizzle’s radiant glow dimming.

His kite, or his friend?

Pella nudged Drizzle, urging retreat. He watched the kite flutter, then turned away, helping Drizzle flee. As they shot off, the ochre clouds below pulsed with an icy chill.

Ever since then, Pella’s marsh stayed damp. It felt a little brighter all the same. The brightest things, he found, were not always made of fabric.
characters: Pella (a marsh rat), Drizzle (a cloud jelly alien)
